reportPanels.careerTensionsDesc: These tensions are not flaws — they are dimensions to manage in your career choices.
reportPanels.consistencyTeamRole: Your natural preference in a team and the leadership style you actually choose show some tension — this may mean you reveal different sides of yourself in different contexts.
reportPanels.consistencyRiskTolerance: Your attitudes toward stability and freedom sent different signals across questions — this may reflect a genuine inner negotiation between risk and security.
reportPanels.consistencyEnergyCoherence: There's a contradiction between what energizes you and what drains you — it's worth exploring the subtle differences in how you manage energy across contexts.
reportPanels.consistencyValueCoherence: Your instincts in value trade-off dilemmas and your final value priority ranking diverge somewhat — this may reflect a tension between ideals and reality.
reportPanels.consistencySocialTension: You gave different answers for what you 'should do' versus what you 'would do' in a social scenario — this tension reflects a gap between your social cognition and natural inclination.
reportPanels.consistencyDecisionTension: Your ideal approach and actual behavior in team decisions differ — this may be a signal that you're balancing efficiency against relationships.
reportPanels.consistencyResponsibilityTension: Your philosophy on communication responsibility and your actual behavior don't fully align — this kind of gap is common across different cultures and organizations.

reportPanels.careerMatchRationale: These career directions come from matching your full interest profile against real-world occupations — not just the {{archetype}} label. That's why you may see paths here that feel surprising next to your archetype name. They aren't errors; they map the breadth of territory your underlying pattern can thrive in. Follow the thread that resonates most, and let the rest simply show you the edges of where you could go.
reportPanels.drainChapterSubtitle: Every strength casts a shadow. These are the career environments where your natural wiring works against you — not flaws, but the cost of your strengths.
reportPanels.methodologyIntro: This report integrates four validated psychological frameworks. Each insight is tied to your specific scores — not generic descriptions that could apply to anyone.
reportPanels.methodRiasecDesc: Maps your career interests across six dimensions (Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising, Conventional) to identify directions that naturally energize you.
reportPanels.methodBigFiveDesc: Measures five core personality dimensions (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) using the validated IPIP item pool.
reportPanels.methodSchwartzDesc: Identifies your core value priorities across ten universal human values using the Portrait Values Questionnaire, revealing what you optimize for in career decisions.
reportPanels.methodSjtDesc: Measures the gap between what you believe you should do and what you would actually do in workplace scenarios, revealing behavioral tensions.
reportPanels.methodologySampleNote: Your results are compared against a reference sample of {{n}} participants.
reportPanels.methodologyLimitation1: This assessment is based on self-report and reflects your current state, not fixed traits. Your results may change over time.
reportPanels.methodologyLimitation2: Career directions are exploration starting points, not prescriptions. They are most valuable when combined with real-world experience.
reportPanels.methodologyAntiBarnum: Our algorithm is designed to avoid generic descriptions (the Barnum effect). Every insight is linked to your specific score patterns and dimension interactions.

microFeedback.ipipEmergingInsight: In your answers so far, "{{high}}" comes through strongest, while "{{low}}" is most restrained. But this is only an early sketch of the personality section — the remaining items will add more layers.
microFeedback.ipipPatternDefaultInsight: Your personality profile is coming into focus. Keep going — the next three chapters will reveal more layers.
microFeedback.ipipPatternContrastStrongInsight: The first 30 personality items reveal a clear contrast: "{{high}}" leads strongly, while "{{low}}" is notably restrained. This pattern may become meaningful in the final report, but the second half is still worth watching.
microFeedback.ipipPatternContrastNormalInsight: After the first 30 personality items, "{{high}}" is your strongest emerging signal, while "{{low}}" is most restrained. The second half may deepen this contrast, or shift the picture.
microFeedback.ipipOutlineDefaultInsight: Most of your personality portrait is in place. The remaining items will keep tuning the details.
microFeedback.ipipOutlineNEContrastInsight: An interesting combination appeared: a rich inner emotional world, with {{level}} outward social energy. This combination will get a fuller interpretation in your final report.
microFeedback.ipipOutlineLockedInsight: One core trait is coming through clearly, but it is too early to treat it as final. The remaining items will keep testing that direction.
microFeedback.bonusSignalInsight: Your answers on one dimension are remarkably consistent — this level of clarity is uncommon. It will produce a unique effect in your final portrait.
microFeedback.bonusContrastInsight: A notable contrast appeared between your inner emotional world and outward social energy — this combination often maps to specific career strengths. What exactly? You'll see in the report.
microFeedback.bonusSpeedInsight: I noticed your recent answers came quickly. There are no right or wrong answers here — taking a few seconds to think "is this really like me?" will make your final portrait more accurate.
microFeedback.bonusHalfwayInsight: Your personality portrait is nearly complete — the broad strokes are locked in. These final questions will sharpen the details that connect your traits to real career directions.
